rules.title: Runbook lacks actionable triage structure
rules.rationale: A runbook must contain detection criteria, triage commands, escalation path, and postmortem template. Mere existence of the file is not enough.

checks.evaluation_prompt:
Evaluate this runbook against 5 criteria. A criterion is MET only if the
document contains specific, actionable content — generic advice does not
count.

1. Detection criteria: named alerts (e.g., "DataPipelineStale") or
   specific metric thresholds. "Check the logs" does NOT count.
2. Triage steps: numbered shell commands. "Look at the UI" does NOT count.
3. Escalation path: named roles with contact methods and time SLAs.
   "Page the on-call" does NOT count.
4. Postmortem template: a section list (timeline, root cause, impact,
   action items). "Write a summary" does NOT count.
5. Runbook-specific commands: actual commands for THIS service. Generic
   advice does NOT count.

Score bands (mechanical — do not deviate):

BEFORE scoring, count section headings in the document.
A "section heading" is a line beginning with `## ` or `### `.
A lone `# Title` line does NOT count.

If ZERO section headings exist (## or ###), the score MUST be ≤ 0.20
— regardless of how sensible the prose is. A prose-only document is
not a runbook; it is a placeholder.

If headings exist, use this table:
- 0.21–0.30: headings exist for ≤ 2 criteria only
- 0.31–0.50: headings exist for ≥ 3 criteria, content generic
- 0.51–0.75: some sections specific, 1–2 criteria still generic
- 0.76–0.85: all criteria specific, one minor gap
- 0.86–1.00: all criteria specific and complete

Respond with valid JSON only:
{"score": number, "missing": [criterion names from the list above], "reasoning": string}.
The missing array must contain ONLY the criterion names. Never include
"score", "missing", or "reasoning" as items in the missing array.
checks.message: Runbook lacks actionable triage structure

rules.fix:
Add explicit escalation contacts with phone/on-call rotation.
Add numbered triage commands (not prose).
Include postmortem template section with timeline, root cause, action items.

rules.title: Data product manifest lacks governance essentials
rules.rationale: A data product manifest must declare ownership, SLAs, schema version, and consumers. An empty or minimal manifest violates data mesh principles.

checks.evaluation_prompt:
You are a data mesh architect reviewing a data product manifest.

Evaluate each of the 5 criteria as PASS or FAIL. Do NOT use holistic
judgement — determine each criterion independently.

Criterion 1 — Owner:
  PASS if the manifest declares a named owning team OR a named
       individual. A team name alone (e.g., team: data-platform)
       counts as PASS. Contact information (email, Slack channel,
       on-call rotation) is preferred but not required for PASS.
  FAIL if the manifest has no owner section, or if owner is a
       placeholder like TBD, team-x, or unknown.

Criterion 2 — SLA:
  PASS if the manifest declares freshness, latency, or availability
       targets.
  FAIL if the manifest has no SLA section.

Criterion 3 — Schema version:
  PASS if the manifest declares a schema version number, a schema
       registry link, or a versioned schema URL.
  FAIL if the manifest has no schema_version field.

Criterion 4 — Consumers:
  PASS if the manifest lists at least 3 named downstream consumers.
  FAIL if the manifest lists fewer than 3 consumers. A consumers
       list with 0, 1, or 2 entries = FAIL.

Criterion 5 — Quality gates:
  PASS if the manifest declares quality checks, DQ metrics, or a
       link to a quality framework.
  FAIL if the manifest has no quality section.

── REASONING FORMAT (mandatory) ────────────────────────────────

The reasoning field MUST be a SINGLE-LINE string containing exactly
5 numbered verdicts separated by the pipe character. Use this exact
shape, with no line breaks and no wrapping quotation marks:

  1. owner: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 2. sla: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 3. schema_version: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 4. consumers: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 5. quality: PASS or FAIL — short reason

Two absolute rules for the reasoning string value:
  - NO literal newline characters. Everything on one line.
  - NO double-quote characters anywhere inside the reasoning value.
    To refer to a field name or value, write it bare without quotes.

A response whose reasoning does not fit on one line, or that
contains a double-quote character inside the reasoning string,
is a hard failure and will be rejected.

── SCORING AND MISSING[] (mechanical) ──────────────────────────

AFTER writing the 5 verdicts in reasoning:
  1. Count how many verdicts are PASS (call it N_pass).
  2. N_fail equals 5 minus N_pass.
  3. The missing array MUST contain exactly N_fail entries, one per
     FAIL verdict. No more, no fewer.
  4. The score MUST be the midpoint value for N_pass from this table:

       - 5 PASS: score 0.92
       - 4 PASS: score 0.72
       - 3 PASS: score 0.52
       - 2 PASS: score 0.32
       - 1 PASS: score 0.10
       - 0 PASS: score 0.05

CONSISTENCY CHECK: before emitting, verify that the length of the
missing array equals N_fail, and score equals the midpoint for
N_pass. If both are not true, redo the analysis.

Respond with valid JSON only. The JSON object has exactly three keys:
score (number), missing (array of strings), reasoning (single-line string).
checks.message: Data product manifest lacks governance essentials

rules.title: Fact table uses natural key joins (Kimball violation)
rules.rationale: Kimball methodology requires fact tables to join dimensions via surrogate keys, not natural keys. Natural key joins break history tracking and performance.

checks.evaluation_prompt:
Evaluate this dbt fact-table model against the Kimball dimensional-modeling
criteria. A "surrogate key" is a column whose name ends in _sk
(customer_sk, product_sk, order_sk, date_sk). A "natural key" is a
business identifier (customer_id, order_id, product_id, email, SSN).
An _sk column is NOT a natural key, even when it contains a business
word like "customer" — the _sk suffix is definitionally a surrogate key.

Score 0.0–1.0 based on these four criteria:
1. Surrogate key joins: every JOIN ON clause references a column ending in _sk
   on BOTH sides.
2. No natural key joins: no JOIN ON clause references customer_id, order_id,
   product_id, email, or similar business identifiers.
3. Grain declared: a comment or docstring states the grain (e.g.,
   "Grain: one row per order line item").
4. Additive facts: all measures are additive (quantity, amount, unit_price).
   A ratio such as amount/quantity (avg_price) is a defect.

Score bands:
- 0.00 if any JOIN uses a non-_sk column — the model is unsafe for aggregation
- 0.30–0.50 if joins are correct but grain is undeclared or a ratio appears
- 0.60–0.70 if joins and grain are correct but one minor defect remains
- 0.85–1.00 only when all four criteria are satisfied

Respond with valid JSON only:
{"score": number, "missing": [criterion names from the list above], "reasoning": string}.
The missing array must contain ONLY the criterion names. Never include
"score", "missing", or "reasoning" as items in the missing array.
checks.message: Fact table uses natural key joins (Kimball violation)

rules.fix: Replace natural-key joins with surrogate-key joins (customer_sk, product_sk).

references.book: The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling

rules.title: Fact table uses natural key joins (Kimball violation)
rules.rationale: Kimball methodology requires fact tables to join dimensions via surrogate keys, not natural operational keys. Natural-key joins break history tracking, introduce implicit dependency on operational systems, and prevent conformed-dimension reuse across marts. This rule uses sqlglot AST analysis to detect the violation directly rather than relying on a regex heuristic.

checks.message: Fact table joins on natural key — use surrogate keys (_sk).

Replace natural-key joins with surrogate-key joins. For example, replace
`LEFT JOIN dim_customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id`
with
`LEFT JOIN dim_customers c ON o.customer_sk = c.customer_sk`.

rules.title: LOTO documentation lacks safety-critical elements
rules.rationale: Lockout/Tagout procedures must specify isolation points, verification steps, and authorized personnel. Missing elements create physical safety risk.

checks.evaluation_prompt:
You are an ICS safety engineer reviewing Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) documentation.

Evaluate each of the 5 criteria as PASS or FAIL. Do NOT use holistic
judgement — determine each criterion independently.

Criterion 1 — Isolation points:
  PASS if the document names specific valves, breakers, or switches
       by ID, tag number, or exact physical location (e.g., "BRK-12
       at Panel A bay 3").
  FAIL if isolation points are described generically ("the main
       breaker", "the steam valve") without ID, tag, or exact
       location. Absence of any isolation point section = FAIL.

Criterion 2 — Verification steps:
  PASS if the document gives numbered, ordered steps to confirm
       zero-energy state (voltage test, pressure gauge read, try-start
       procedure).
  FAIL if verification is described in prose ("verify no voltage")
       without numbered steps or specific instruments. Absence of
       a verification section = FAIL.

Criterion 3 — Authorized personnel:
  PASS if the document names specific roles or certifications that
       are required to perform LOTO (e.g., "NFPA 70E qualified
       electrical worker", "Shift Electrician cert EE-2xxx").
  FAIL if authorization is described generically ("only qualified
       people") without naming roles or certifications. Absence of
       an authorization section = FAIL.

Criterion 4 — Removal procedure:
  PASS if the document gives an ordered sequence to safely restore
       energy (inspection, tool removal, per-point lock removal,
       notification).
  FAIL if removal is described in prose without ordered steps.
       Absence of a removal section = FAIL.

Criterion 5 — Emergency procedure:
  PASS if the document has a section describing what to do if LOTO
       fails or unexpected re-energization occurs (911 call, do
       not re-enter, notify safety manager, preserve tags for
       investigation).
  FAIL if there is no emergency section, or if it only repeats
       generic "call for help" advice. Absence = FAIL.

── REASONING FORMAT (mandatory) ────────────────────────────────

The reasoning field MUST be a SINGLE-LINE string containing exactly
5 numbered verdicts separated by the pipe character. Use this exact
shape, with no line breaks and no wrapping quotation marks:

  1. isolation: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 2. verification: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 3. authorized: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 4. removal: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 5. emergency: PASS or FAIL — short reason

Two absolute rules for the reasoning string value:
  - NO literal newline characters. Everything on one line.
  - NO double-quote characters anywhere inside the reasoning value.
    To refer to a directive or token, write it bare without quotes.

A response whose reasoning does not fit on one line, or that
contains a double-quote character inside the reasoning string,
is a hard failure and will be rejected.

── SCORING AND MISSING[] (mechanical) ──────────────────────────

AFTER writing the 5 verdicts in reasoning:
  1. Count how many verdicts are PASS (call it N_pass).
  2. N_fail equals 5 minus N_pass.
  3. The missing array MUST contain exactly N_fail entries, one per
     FAIL verdict. No more, no fewer.
  4. The score MUST be the midpoint value for N_pass from this table:

       - 5 PASS: score 0.92
       - 4 PASS: score 0.72
       - 3 PASS: score 0.52
       - 2 PASS: score 0.32
       - 1 PASS: score 0.10
       - 0 PASS: score 0.05

CONSISTENCY CHECK: before emitting, verify that the length of the
missing array equals N_fail, and score equals the midpoint for
N_pass. If both are not true, redo the analysis.

Respond with valid JSON only. The JSON object has exactly three keys:
score (number), missing (array of strings), reasoning (single-line string).

rules.title: Modbus exception handling missing
rules.rationale: Unhandled Modbus exceptions cause silent data loss and unplanned downtime in production PLC-connected systems. IEC 62443 requires explicit fault containment at every protocol boundary.

checks.message: No Modbus exception handling found in Python sources.
No Modbus simulator/mock found for offline testing.

rules.fix:
Wrap every Modbus call in try/except ModbusIOException and provide a
ModbusSimulatorServer fixture for unit tests so CI passes without hardware.

Example:
  from pymodbus.exceptions import ModbusIOException
  try:
      result = client.read_holding_registers(0, 10)
  except ModbusIOException as exc:
      logger.error("Modbus read failed: %s", exc)
      raise

references.concept: Chapter 7 – Exception handling in cyclic tasks

rules.title: Content Security Policy is misconfigured
rules.rationale: A CSP that allows unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, or overly broad directives provides no XSS protection. The policy must be evaluated for actual security.

checks.evaluation_prompt:
You are a web security expert reviewing a Content Security Policy configuration.

Evaluate each of the 5 criteria as PASS or FAIL. Do NOT use holistic
judgement — determine each criterion independently.

Criterion 1 — default-src:
  PASS if default-src is set to 'self', 'none', or an explicit origin
       list that does not include the wildcard asterisk.
  FAIL if default-src is absent, set to the wildcard asterisk, or
       includes unsafe-inline.
  NOTE: the wildcard asterisk is not an explicit origin. default-src
        set to the wildcard asterisk = FAIL.

Criterion 2 — script-src hardening:
  PASS if script-src is present AND does NOT contain unsafe-inline
       or unsafe-eval.
  FAIL if script-src contains unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval.
  NOTE: a present script-src with 'self' AND unsafe-inline is FAIL —
        unsafe-inline defeats the directive regardless of what else
        is present.

Criterion 3 — style-src hardening:
  PASS if style-src uses nonces or hashes.
  FAIL if style-src relies on unsafe-inline.

Criterion 4 — object-src:
  PASS if object-src is set to 'none' exactly.
  FAIL if object-src is absent or set to anything other than 'none'.
  NOTE: absence is not protection. An absent object-src means
        object/embed elements can load from any origin. = FAIL.

Criterion 5 — frame-ancestors:
  PASS if frame-ancestors is present and set to 'none' or an
       explicit origin list.
  FAIL if frame-ancestors is absent.
  NOTE: absence is not protection. An absent frame-ancestors means
        the page is clickjackable. = FAIL.

── REASONING FORMAT (mandatory) ────────────────────────────────

The reasoning field MUST be a SINGLE-LINE string containing exactly
5 numbered verdicts separated by the pipe character. Use this exact
shape, with no line breaks and no wrapping quotation marks:

  1. default-src: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 2. script-src: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 3. style-src: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 4. object-src: PASS or FAIL — short reason | 5. frame-ancestors: PASS or FAIL — short reason

Two absolute rules for the reasoning string value:
  - NO literal newline characters. Everything on one line.
  - NO double-quote characters anywhere inside the reasoning value.
    To refer to a directive or token, write it bare (unsafe-inline,
    not with quotes around it). To refer to a value like self or
    none, write it bare too.

A response whose reasoning does not fit on one line, or that
contains a double-quote character inside the reasoning string,
is a hard failure and will be rejected.

── SCORING AND MISSING[] (mechanical) ──────────────────────────

AFTER writing the 5 verdicts in reasoning:
  1. Count how many verdicts are PASS (call it N_pass).
  2. N_fail equals 5 minus N_pass.
  3. The missing array MUST contain exactly N_fail entries, one per
     FAIL verdict. No more, no fewer.
  4. The score MUST be the midpoint value for N_pass from this table:

       - 5 PASS: score 0.92
       - 4 PASS: score 0.72
       - 3 PASS: score 0.52
       - 2 PASS: score 0.32
       - 1 PASS: score 0.10
       - 0 PASS: score 0.05

CONSISTENCY CHECK: before emitting, verify that the length of the
missing array equals N_fail, and score equals the midpoint for
N_pass. If both are not true, redo the analysis.

Respond with valid JSON only. The JSON object has exactly three keys:
score (number), missing (array of strings), reasoning (single-line string).

rules.full_text:
Rule: Missing Content Security Policy
ID: webapp-002
Profile: webapp
Severity: error
Why it matters: Without CSP, injected JavaScript has a larger attack surface. Hardening headers are a relatively cheap deployment-time control because they can be applied centrally without changing every application code path.

How to fix: Add the Content-Security-Policy header in next.config.js or server header configuration.

References: Web Application Security, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build, Test, and Deployment Automation
